Lowveld Hijacked?

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fact finding mission to Pilgrim's Rest to investigate zama zama activity leads to an alarming expose' - has the Lowveld been hijacked by illegal miners?

Unique Selling Point:
We spent a day in the sleepy tourist town of Pilgrim's rest, where our producer went undercover as a tourist taking in the sights. We'd heard reports of zama activity in the area, and that the situation had become dangerous for tourists.

Although Pilgrim's is by no means overrun by zama zamas, they can be found in the town, processing gold bearing material at the river just 500 meters away from the main tourist attractions.

But our producer dug a little a deeper, and has uncovered that the illegal mining problem in the Lowveld is possibly even bigger than what residents in places like Guateng's West and East Rand are dealing with.

With the surge in zama activity, major tourist hotspots in the Lowveld are on the brink of disaster - as the illegal mining in the area has caused a sharp increase in violent crimes, and just as concerning, a major ecological threat to our natural heritage in the area. Illegal miners are constructing so called "Cyanide Baths" next to important waterways such as the Sabie and Crocodile river, using deadly poisons such as cyanide in the process of processing the gold ore.

Summary:
We have access to never before seen areas where large scale zama zama activities are taking place in the Lowveld.
We have been given a lot of exclusive footage of zama operations as well.
We have access to sources working on intelligence gathering on zama operations - who can open this hidden world.

We will show the scale of the problems in areas such as Nelspruit, Sabie, Pilgrim's Rest, Waterval Onder and Barberton. In e each town we have insiders who can give us exclusive access into the hidden world of the zamas.

Further information:
We will be working with insiders, private security and intelligence personnel.

We have access to drone footage from private security

We have access to a helicopter to reach inaccessible areas in the mountains around towns like Nelspruit where Zamas operate.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel and accomodation for crew and presenter for 5 days.

Lowveld Hijacked
SECOND Draft Script
Monday 31 October 2024
Intro
Aerials and music
Voice
The Lowveld in Mpumalanga.
It’s hard to imagine a place blessed with more natural beauty.
Aerials and music
Voice
But its natural abundance is both its biggest asset and its darkest curse. Home to world
heritage sites, vast farms and plantations, the Lowveld is also a place where two worlds
collide… an entire region hijacked for the riches hiding beneath the surface.
Ups Masa
I can’t even see the bottom.
Fade to Black
Act 1
TITLE: PILGRIM’S REST
Link Masa
Pilgrim’s Rest - a popular destination for tourists both local and international, it’s a gem in South
Africa. But a stone’s throw away, we have this, illegal activity in broad daylight.
Voice
We’ve come to Pilgrim’s Rest to investigate claims the town is slowly dying, and the
damaged riverbed running alongside it hints at who’s to blame. It’s caused by Zama Zamas,
the notorious syndicates running much of the country’s illicit mining.
Locals here are understandably worried about the impact of the reports on tourism, so we
sent our producer undercover to get a sense of the scale of the problem. Wearing a hidden
camera, he heard about the impact of illegal mining.
Ups Hiddencam
Man: They just chased them from around the stream, now they’re mining behind this mountain.
Actually there’s a mine behind this mountain.
Voice
The Zama Zamas are now mining right alongside the town’s main tourist strip, site of the
country’s first gold rush in 1873.
Ups Hiddencam
Man: Zama zamas?
Producer: Ja.
Man: Big time. If you look to the river down this side…
Producer: Ja
Man: Check at how much they’ve pulled the banks away from where that little stream used to be,
it’s now almost a river.
Producer: Genuine hey? So it is an issue?
Man: Ja, ja. Even myself, I won’t go out into that section by myself with my camera.
Producer: Like where, just across the road here?
Man: Just inside here. I won’t go there by myself, unless there’s somebody with me. Especially at
night. At night they say you don’t go anywhere near that side.
Producer: Really hey?
Voice
But a story about a small tourist town struggling under the impacts of illegal mining turned
into something far bigger than we’d imagined.
We returned to the area
-
this time with a full crew.
As we dig deeper, we’re taken on a journey across the Lowveld and discover illicit mining
on a grand scale; where vast tracts have been turned into a pockmarked and poisoned
wasteland.
Voice
Sabie, about 35 km’s from Pilgrim’s rest, is no exception. Francois Oberholzer speaks for
the areas forestry sector
–
a major contributor to the local and national economy but now
virtually locked out from its operations by the Zamas.
Upsound Francois Oberholzer
It’s becoming an increasingly big problem. We sit with approximately 496 000 hectares of land
holding just in Mpumalanga alone. And we’re not not like agriculture where you can fence a
property. So most of our properties are unfenced. So people have got easy access.
Voice
Mining is even taking place around the roots of trees that have stood here for decades.
Upsound Francois
Just the fact that these zama zamas are getting away with the amount of mining that they
do on our land, land we don’t have access to anymore, shows that there’s not such a big
focus on these environmental crimes as it should be.
Upsound smelting
Voice
Extracting the final product from the subterranean rock isn’t easy.
Gold is mostly mined underground where the syndicates use black market explosives to get
to the ore.
That, and the fact that many Zamas carry weapons, makes policing illegal mining extremely
dangerous work.
TITLE: SABIE
Upsound Gerhard Van Staden Contract Manager Phoenix Flying Squad
Masa: I’m just glad that we have a nice big car to do all of this in.
Gerhard: You need 4x4 for this country.
Masa: It’s nice and rugged.
Gerhard: And this valley especially, this is the Lowveld.
Voice
Still in Sabie, we meet Gerhard van Staden, from a local security company protecting the
interests of the forestry industry.
He drives us to the notoriously dangerous South Shaft, about 10 minutes outside town.
Upsound Gerhard
old.
Gerhard: I’ve found a small group of boys, about 6 or 7 boys, between he ages of 12 and 16 years
Masa: 12…
Gerhard: That I’ve taken to the police station and that we helped to relocate them to a safe haven.
Masa: 12!
Gerhard: 12 years old. Illegal mining. Digging, working underground. Being forced, for labour.
Voice
When South Shaft shut down, the mine covered it with a thick layer of concrete
-
but that
didn’t stop the zamas. An underground river that crosses the shaft feeds into the town’s
water supply.
Upsound Gerhard
Gerhard: If they kill a person underground, for forced labour or disobedience or anything in that
form, like they’ve done on this road, I’ll show you now, they just throw it into another shaft and it’s
being left there to decompose completely.
Masa: And that water…
Upsound Gerhard: Is feeding Sabie’s main water.
Masa: Ewww.
Voice
This bullet riddled body was recently found just up the road.
Upsound Gerhard
Masa: So this is the entrance?
Gerhard: Yes, you can see here it’s been closed oﬀ with rocks, we barricaded it oﬀ completely, we
tried to make it as diﬃcult as possible, and within 48 hours it was reopened and they gained
access again.
Gerhard: I’m taking Ronald with us-
Masa: Dumela Ronald
Gerhard: …because he’s been in before, and myself have been in before, we’re both armed and
we know how to do…
Masa: I trust you and Ronald
Gerhard: Should there be someone waiting (laughs)
Masa: (Laughs) should there be someone waiting.
Voice
Despite the laughter, entering an abandoned mine shaft controlled by armed Zama Zamas
is risky.
Upsound Masa
Masa: I feel like I should say bye bye to the real world, and go into an underworld. Oh my
goodness this is insane!
Gerhard: Ja just the first bit - it gets bigger I promise!
Masa: And the elbow?
Gerhard: Ja this is your elbow. So here’s your anchor point, where they will anchor themselves
with a rope, and I see they’ve made anew one there, and this is your shaft.
Masa: Let’s see. Wow, wow, wow, that is deep! I can’t even see the bottom.
Voice
We’re told it’s 100 meters deep
–
that’s roughly the height of a 30-story building. Zamas
descend shafts like these by rope, into the chaos below.
Upsound Zamas underground footage
Link Masa
The life of an illegal miner is something else - it’s scary. I mean this place is old, it’s dark, and it’s
definitely dangerous. Add to that, they’re using rudimentary equipment - a life can be lost, just like
that.
Voice
They don’t take kindly to intruders either. While we haven’t seen anyone down here…
Upsound Hear hammer noises.
Voice
…we can hear them working deep below us. It’s time to leave.
Upsound Gerhard
Gerhard: I’ve never been into the shaft, and I never will.
Masa: I’m with you on that.
Upsound Masa exits hole
Oh my gosh, it’s crazy down there. Whoever said our jobs are glamorous, they need to see this
part.
Act 2
More Upsound smelting
Voice
Once the ore bearing material has been blasted from the rockface, it needs to be crushed
into a fine powder.
This footage shows what is known as a “wash plant”, the gold is separated from the
powder using makeshift tumblers called “pendukas” that are filled with ball bearings and
dangerous chemicals like Mercury.
And the Zamas stop at nothing to protect these operations.
Upsound Gerhard
Gerhard: Live ammunition.
Masa: Oh my gosh I didn’t see that, I saw the R1 coin.
Voice
At South Shaft, we find an eerie reminder of the violence that surrounds this underworld.
Upsound Gerhard
Masa: So any minute now, there could be shots?
Gerhard: Yes because you’re here, vulnerable. At this very point. All around us it’s massive lookout
points.
Masa: Chances are they are watching us right now?
Gerhard: For a fact.
Voice
Not long after our visit, Gerhard’s team and police were in a shootout with armed zamas at
this very spot. They recovered a cache of weapons and ammunition including 1500 AK47
rounds
-
enough to stock a small army.
It’s a surprising level of firepower in an area now more famous for its wood than its gold.
Upsound Gerhard
Masa: So this is an active forestry area?
Gerhard: Yes correct, this is active forestry area. These trees if I have to guess are anything
between 8 and 12 years old. We have to keep looking after them up until the age of 20/22 years
where it’s then primed for harvesting.
Voice
Protecting the trees is a challenge in an area now bearing the signature scars of illicit
mining.
Upsound Gerhard
So they’ll dig down to a certain depth, and then they’ll vein it out at the bottom. Then it’s like veins
going in diﬀerent directions from the bottom point going outwards.
Voice
This entire area is riddled with similar shafts
-
but we only see the true and terrifying scale
of the problem on a nearby hillside.
MUSIC AND AERIALS
Voice
Coming up in part two of our special report…
Upsound Gerhard
Okay - rules of engagement, only shoot when shot at…
Voice
In terrain that makes clamping down on the Zamas a near impossible task…
Upsound Masa
And they’re just clearing out the road that’s been blocked by the zama zamas. As we were coming
in, we could see them on the mountain tops as well. This area is called Gold Reef City because
their’s a gold processing illegal facility here.
ACTION SHOTS NEEDED
…we trek deep into the mountains with law enforcement as they swoop on an illegal gold
processing facility.
PART 1 ENDS
PART 2
Upsound Cars drive
Upsound Gerhard Driving
It looks a lot like The Wrong Turn…
Upsound Gerhard security briefing
Only shoot when shot at. We’re not going to turn around and retreat, otherwise they’re going to
give us a surprise from behind and we don’t want that.
Voice
An early morning raid is about to take place on a secret gold processing facility deep in the
mountains between Sabie and Pilgrim’s Rest in Mpumalanga.
Continue UPS
And the we will clear the area, and then take control of it. Okay?
New Voice
We’re following up on reports that Zama Zamas are holding vast swathes of the Lowveld to
ransom. Illegal mining is threatening tourism and local industries like forestry are finding it
increasingly hard to operate. It’s a journey that’ll eventually take us underground with the
Zama Zamas…
Upsound Zama takes Masa Underground
Don’t be scared mama, come through.
Voice
…but right now, our priority is staying out of danger.
Upsound Gerhard
Let’s go guys, move, move, move.
This is where they started blocking the roads.
Upsound Masa
We’ve just entered an area dubbed “Gold Reef City”, we’re here with private security and law
enforcement and they’re just clearing out the road that’s been blocked by the zama zamas. As we
were coming in we could see them on the mountain tops as well. There’s a gold processing illegal
facility here.
Voice
The zamas have chosen their location well - it’s a kilometre's trek over rough terrain.
Upsound Masa
It is volatile, it is dangerous, we can see the zamas on the mountains, and as you can hear I’m out
of breath. It is a lot of work.
Upsound Masa
Masa: Do they hide in here?
Police man: Ja they do.
Voice
We arrive to an empty camp: The zamas have melted into the surrounding hills without a
shot fired…. an abandoned campfire still burning.
Security have caught a lone suspect as he tried to escape, but other than telling us he’s
from Mozambique, he’s giving little away.
Upsound Masa
So one alleged illegal miner has been apprehended, he claims he only arrived in South Africa
yesterday, he has no documentation, and no passport on him.
Voice
Hidden amongst the dense undergrowth, we find what looks to be at least a ton of gold bearing
material, pendukas, and gas bottles used for smelting. Two so called “acid baths” are situated
right next to the river. Further upstream the zamas seem to have built a dam to control the water
flow.
Final UPS from Manufacturing Process
Voice
Bigger Zama operations use “acid baths” where highly volatile and even deadly chemicals
like cyanide are added to the mix to separate the gold from the ore.
In the final stage, gold concentrate will be brought to smelting houses like these where the
resulting nugget can sell at upwards of R1000 per gram at Zama prices.
Upsound Masa
This is a precious natural resource area - but look at the state it’s in.
Upsound destroy camp
Voice
Security do what they can to disrupt the operation
–
unable to catch them, they try to
discourage them from coming back.
Upsound destroy camp and fire
Voice
As this illegal camp goes up in flames, 60 kms away, close to Mpumalanga’s capital,
another is flourishing.
Upsound Mongezi Mlambo
The kinds of guns that these guys carry, it’s the kinds of guns that you’ll see on Rambo. Or on big
action movies.
Voice
In Mashabotho - just outside Mbombela - a rural community is living in fear.
Upsound Mongezi Mlambo
Sometimes you have to pass through the bushes, because you can’t use an open road. Because
they will see you from far, and attack you.
Voice
People here make a humble living from working a farm government handed back to them
after a successful land claim.
Upsound Mongezi
It was just the communities and the beneficiaries living here. It was peaceful.
Voice
Mashabotho local, Mongezi Mlambo, says a nearby hillside, part of their land, has been
invaded by zamas, interrupting their plans to get the farm up and running.
Upsound Mongezi
goes up?
Masa: The crime aspect, would you say that as the zamas increase in the area the crime also
Mongezi: It’s the reason why there’s crime.
Voice
It’s a view we’ve encountered all over the Lowveld: where Zama Zamas gather, crime
inevitably increases.
Upsound Mongezi
Mongezi: We had local spazas here that were operating, all these things closed because of these
guys. So these guys will come and own that place. Sort of like remove you from that place and
say ok, from today, you’re no longer occupying here. If we find you tomorrow we’re gonna abuse
you up until you on your own say I no longer want to continue.
Masa: Tell us how that has impacted this community?
Mongezi: It has destroyed a lot of lives. Day and night, they are not safe.
Voice
Eager to get a glimpse of the operation that’s brought business here to a halt, we attempt to
negotiate our way up the hillside.
Link Masa
Up on this mountain there are literally hundreds of zamas operating - we also wanted to hear their
side of the story - but the syndicate leaders didn’t give us permission. Instead, they sent two men
down here to meet with us.
Voice
One of them, whose name is Surprise, agrees to talk to us. He’s left behind a corporate life
for the better paying Zama life.
Upsound “Surprise”
Masa: Did you study?
Surprise: Yes, I did study.
Masa: What did you study?
Surprise: Oﬃce administration.
Masa: Oﬃce administration. And you work underground?
Surprise: I am happy because I’ve got like certain targets that I have to reach, but I’m going to do
it temporarily, it’s not going to be forever you see.
Voice
He tells us there’s more gold available here than in Gauteng.
Upsound Surpise
Masa: How much money do you make out of this on average?
Surprise: Last week we were working, and then we are going to be coming out this Saturday - so
it’s going to be two weeks full that we’re working, so maybe plus minus R20 000 for me. And
we’re a syndicate you see.
Upsound Mongezi
There are big guys that are benefitting from this, and that is why whenever you report such cases,
they always go unsolved.
Voice
Mongezi believes powerful people are shielding the Zamas from justice. Surprise might
make 20 thousand, but the syndicate bosses make far more.
Upsound Mongezi
Because of the involvement of very influential people from within the country. Which is the
sad story.
Upsound Surpise
Masa: Everywhere where there’s communities living where the zamas are as well, they’re living in
fear. They’re saying as zamas you’re disturbing them. You’re actually harassing them. What do
you say to that?
Surprise: On the bad side of it is like we are working with illegal people, we’ve got like
ammunition, and obviously when we’re digging, obviously even us, we have to explode… so
obviously it disturbs the people that are not used to such type of a vibe of maybe explosions,
guns triggering every now and then.
Masa: And the zama’s here, you don’t think they harass the community members here?
Surpise: No, they don’t harass the community members here.
ACT 3
Voice
This area is the country’s second biggest producer of citrus fruits and the “acid baths” used
by the zamas are threatening water sources vital to the sector’s survival.
And, as we discover first hand in Barberton, a little over 40 kms away, famed World Heritage
Sites aren’t being spared either.
Upsound Masa
How much further?
Voice
history.
Famous for its gold mines and as the home of Jock of the Bushveld, Baberton has a rich cultural
Upsound Masa
One thing about the zama world, there’s a lot of walking, you need to be fit.
Voice
We’re trekking up a mountain just outside the town, following a pair of illegal miners who’ve
agreed to show us their operations.
Upsound Masa
Masa: Welcome to zama zama land.
Zama: Don’t run away, we spoke to security when we arrived.
Link Masa
It’s not that easy entering the world of the zama zamas. There’s a lot of layers to get through to
get the permission to be in this space. Right now, there are zamas on the mountain as we’re
waiting to get our final permission. They say while we can’t see them - we can hear them - they all
can see us.
Voice
We’ve arrived without any security, but the Zamas are still nervous: their camp was raided
just a few days ago.
Upsound Zama
Zama: The police destroyed it.
Masa: When? Monday?
Zama: This was Monday.
Voice
Amidst pendukas broken during the raid, we’re shown how things work.
Upsound Zama
The Mercury collects the gold, then you pick the gold pieces out.
Voice
Then, he takes us below ground.
Upsound Zama
Don’t be scared mama, come through.
Upsound Masa
Masa: So we’re entering the tunnel, where all the digging takes place. He’s just alerting the other

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission Proposal Show: Carte Blanche One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A fact finding mission to Pilgrim's Rest to investigate zama zama activity leads to an alarming expose' - has the Lowveld been hijacked by illegal miners? Unique Selling Point: We spent a day in the sleepy tourist town of Pilgrim's rest, where our producer went undercover as a tourist taking in the sights. We'd heard reports of zama activity in the area, and that the situation had become dangerous for tourists. Although Pilgrim's is by no means overrun by zama zamas, they can be found in the town, processing gold bearing material at the river just 500 meters away from the main tourist attractions. But our producer dug a little a deeper, and has uncovered that the illegal mining problem in the Lowveld is possibly even bigger than what residents in places like Guateng's West and East Rand are dealing with. With the surge in zama activity, major tourist hotspots in the Lowveld are on the brink of disaster - as the illegal mining in the area has caused a sharp increase in violent crimes, and just as concerning, a major ecological threat to our natural heritage in the area. Illegal miners are constructing so called "Cyanide Baths" next to important waterways such as the Sabie and Crocodile river, using deadly poisons such as cyanide in the process of processing the gold ore. Summary: We have access to never before seen areas where large scale zama zama activities are taking place in the Lowveld. We have been given a lot of exclusive footage of zama operations as well. We have access to sources working on intelligence gathering on zama operations - who can open this hidden world. We will show the scale of the problems in areas such as Nelspruit, Sabie, Pilgrim's Rest, Waterval Onder and Barberton. In e each town we have insiders who can give us exclusive access into the hidden world of the zamas. Further information: We will be working with insiders, private security and intelligence personnel. We have access to drone footage from private security We have access to a helicopter to reach inaccessible areas in the mountains around towns like Nelspruit where Zamas operate. Extra Budget Items: Travel and accomodation for crew and presenter for 5 days. Lowveld Hijacked SECOND Draft Script Monday 31 October 2024 Intro Aerials and music Voice The Lowveld in Mpumalanga. It’s hard to imagine a place blessed with more natural beauty. Aerials and music Voice But its natural abundance is both its biggest asset and its darkest curse. Home to world heritage sites, vast farms and plantations, the Lowveld is also a place where two worlds collide… an entire region hijacked for the riches hiding beneath the surface. Ups Masa I can’t even see the bottom. Fade to Black Act 1 TITLE: PILGRIM’S REST Link Masa Pilgrim’s Rest - a popular destination for tourists both local and international, it’s a gem in South Africa. But a stone’s throw away, we have this, illegal activity in broad daylight. Voice We’ve come to Pilgrim’s Rest to investigate claims the town is slowly dying, and the damaged riverbed running alongside it hints at who’s to blame. It’s caused by Zama Zamas, the notorious syndicates running much of the country’s illicit mining. Locals here are understandably worried about the impact of the reports on tourism, so we sent our producer undercover to get a sense of the scale of the problem. Wearing a hidden camera, he heard about the impact of illegal mining. Ups Hiddencam Man: They just chased them from around the stream, now they’re mining behind this mountain. Actually there’s a mine behind this mountain. Voice The Zama Zamas are now mining right alongside the town’s main tourist strip, site of the country’s first gold rush in 1873. Ups Hiddencam Man: Zama zamas? Producer: Ja. Man: Big time. If you look to the river down this side… Producer: Ja Man: Check at how much they’ve pulled the banks away from where that little stream used to be, it’s now almost a river. Producer: Genuine hey? So it is an issue? Man: Ja, ja. Even myself, I won’t go out into that section by myself with my camera. Producer: Like where, just across the road here? Man: Just inside here. I won’t go there by myself, unless there’s somebody with me. Especially at night. At night they say you don’t go anywhere near that side. Producer: Really hey? Voice But a story about a small tourist town struggling under the impacts of illegal mining turned into something far bigger than we’d imagined. We returned to the area - this time with a full crew. As we dig deeper, we’re taken on a journey across the Lowveld and discover illicit mining on a grand scale; where vast tracts have been turned into a pockmarked and poisoned wasteland. Voice Sabie, about 35 km’s from Pilgrim’s rest, is no exception. Francois Oberholzer speaks for the areas forestry sector – a major contributor to the local and national economy but now virtually locked out from its operations by the Zamas. Upsound Francois Oberholzer It’s becoming an increasingly big problem. We sit with approximately 496 000 hectares of land holding just in Mpumalanga alone. And we’re not not like agriculture where you can fence a property. So most of our properties are unfenced. So people have got easy access. Voice Mining is even taking place around the roots of trees that have stood here for decades. Upsound Francois Just the fact that these zama zamas are getting away with the amount of mining that they do on our land, land we don’t have access to anymore, shows that there’s not such a big focus on these environmental crimes as it should be. Upsound smelting Voice Extracting the final product from the subterranean rock isn’t easy. Gold is mostly mined underground where the syndicates use black market explosives to get to the ore. That, and the fact that many Zamas carry weapons, makes policing illegal mining extremely dangerous work. TITLE: SABIE Upsound Gerhard Van Staden Contract Manager Phoenix Flying Squad Masa: I’m just glad that we have a nice big car to do all of this in. Gerhard: You need 4x4 for this country. Masa: It’s nice and rugged. Gerhard: And this valley especially, this is the Lowveld. Voice Still in Sabie, we meet Gerhard van Staden, from a local security company protecting the interests of the forestry industry. He drives us to the notoriously dangerous South Shaft, about 10 minutes outside town. Upsound Gerhard old. Gerhard: I’ve found a small group of boys, about 6 or 7 boys, between he ages of 12 and 16 years Masa: 12… Gerhard: That I’ve taken to the police station and that we helped to relocate them to a safe haven. Masa: 12! Gerhard: 12 years old. Illegal mining. Digging, working underground. Being forced, for labour. Voice When South Shaft shut down, the mine covered it with a thick layer of concrete - but that didn’t stop the zamas. An underground river that crosses the shaft feeds into the town’s water supply. Upsound Gerhard Gerhard: If they kill a person underground, for forced labour or disobedience or anything in that form, like they’ve done on this road, I’ll show you now, they just throw it into another shaft and it’s being left there to decompose completely. Masa: And that water… Upsound Gerhard: Is feeding Sabie’s main water. Masa: Ewww. Voice This bullet riddled body was recently found just up the road. Upsound Gerhard Masa: So this is the entrance? Gerhard: Yes, you can see here it’s been closed oﬀ with rocks, we barricaded it oﬀ completely, we tried to make it as diﬃcult as possible, and within 48 hours it was reopened and they gained access again. Gerhard: I’m taking Ronald with us- Masa: Dumela Ronald Gerhard: …because he’s been in before, and myself have been in before, we’re both armed and we know how to do… Masa: I trust you and Ronald Gerhard: Should there be someone waiting (laughs) Masa: (Laughs) should there be someone waiting. Voice Despite the laughter, entering an abandoned mine shaft controlled by armed Zama Zamas is risky. Upsound Masa Masa: I feel like I should say bye bye to the real world, and go into an underworld. Oh my goodness this is insane! Gerhard: Ja just the first bit - it gets bigger I promise! Masa: And the elbow? Gerhard: Ja this is your elbow. So here’s your anchor point, where they will anchor themselves with a rope, and I see they’ve made anew one there, and this is your shaft. Masa: Let’s see. Wow, wow, wow, that is deep! I can’t even see the bottom. Voice We’re told it’s 100 meters deep – that’s roughly the height of a 30-story building. Zamas descend shafts like these by rope, into the chaos below. Upsound Zamas underground footage Link Masa The life of an illegal miner is something else - it’s scary. I mean this place is old, it’s dark, and it’s definitely dangerous. Add to that, they’re using rudimentary equipment - a life can be lost, just like that. Voice They don’t take kindly to intruders either. While we haven’t seen anyone down here… Upsound Hear hammer noises. Voice …we can hear them working deep below us. It’s time to leave. Upsound Gerhard Gerhard: I’ve never been into the shaft, and I never will. Masa: I’m with you on that. Upsound Masa exits hole Oh my gosh, it’s crazy down there. Whoever said our jobs are glamorous, they need to see this part. Act 2 More Upsound smelting Voice Once the ore bearing material has been blasted from the rockface, it needs to be crushed into a fine powder. This footage shows what is known as a “wash plant”, the gold is separated from the powder using makeshift tumblers called “pendukas” that are filled with ball bearings and dangerous chemicals like Mercury. And the Zamas stop at nothing to protect these operations. Upsound Gerhard Gerhard: Live ammunition. Masa: Oh my gosh I didn’t see that, I saw the R1 coin. Voice At South Shaft, we find an eerie reminder of the violence that surrounds this underworld. Upsound Gerhard Masa: So any minute now, there could be shots? Gerhard: Yes because you’re here, vulnerable. At this very point. All around us it’s massive lookout points. Masa: Chances are they are watching us right now? Gerhard: For a fact. Voice Not long after our visit, Gerhard’s team and police were in a shootout with armed zamas at this very spot. They recovered a cache of weapons and ammunition including 1500 AK47 rounds - enough to stock a small army. It’s a surprising level of firepower in an area now more famous for its wood than its gold. Upsound Gerhard Masa: So this is an active forestry area? Gerhard: Yes correct, this is active forestry area. These trees if I have to guess are anything between 8 and 12 years old. We have to keep looking after them up until the age of 20/22 years where it’s then primed for harvesting. Voice Protecting the trees is a challenge in an area now bearing the signature scars of illicit mining. Upsound Gerhard So they’ll dig down to a certain depth, and then they’ll vein it out at the bottom. Then it’s like veins going in diﬀerent directions from the bottom point going outwards. Voice This entire area is riddled with similar shafts - but we only see the true and terrifying scale of the problem on a nearby hillside. MUSIC AND AERIALS Voice Coming up in part two of our special report… Upsound Gerhard Okay - rules of engagement, only shoot when shot at… Voice In terrain that makes clamping down on the Zamas a near impossible task… Upsound Masa And they’re just clearing out the road that’s been blocked by the zama zamas. As we were coming in, we could see them on the mountain tops as well. This area is called Gold Reef City because their’s a gold processing illegal facility here. ACTION SHOTS NEEDED …we trek deep into the mountains with law enforcement as they swoop on an illegal gold processing facility. PART 1 ENDS PART 2 Upsound Cars drive Upsound Gerhard Driving It looks a lot like The Wrong Turn… Upsound Gerhard security briefing Only shoot when shot at. We’re not going to turn around and retreat, otherwise they’re going to give us a surprise from behind and we don’t want that. Voice An early morning raid is about to take place on a secret gold processing facility deep in the mountains between Sabie and Pilgrim’s Rest in Mpumalanga. Continue UPS And the we will clear the area, and then take control of it. Okay? New Voice We’re following up on reports that Zama Zamas are holding vast swathes of the Lowveld to ransom. Illegal mining is threatening tourism and local industries like forestry are finding it increasingly hard to operate. It’s a journey that’ll eventually take us underground with the Zama Zamas… Upsound Zama takes Masa Underground Don’t be scared mama, come through. Voice …but right now, our priority is staying out of danger. Upsound Gerhard Let’s go guys, move, move, move. This is where they started blocking the roads. Upsound Masa We’ve just entered an area dubbed “Gold Reef City”, we’re here with private security and law enforcement and they’re just clearing out the road that’s been blocked by the zama zamas. As we were coming in we could see them on the mountain tops as well. There’s a gold processing illegal facility here. Voice The zamas have chosen their location well - it’s a kilometre's trek over rough terrain. Upsound Masa It is volatile, it is dangerous, we can see the zamas on the mountains, and as you can hear I’m out of breath. It is a lot of work. Upsound Masa Masa: Do they hide in here? Police man: Ja they do. Voice We arrive to an empty camp: The zamas have melted into the surrounding hills without a shot fired…. an abandoned campfire still burning. Security have caught a lone suspect as he tried to escape, but other than telling us he’s from Mozambique, he’s giving little away. Upsound Masa So one alleged illegal miner has been apprehended, he claims he only arrived in South Africa yesterday, he has no documentation, and no passport on him. Voice Hidden amongst the dense undergrowth, we find what looks to be at least a ton of gold bearing material, pendukas, and gas bottles used for smelting. Two so called “acid baths” are situated right next to the river. Further upstream the zamas seem to have built a dam to control the water flow. Final UPS from Manufacturing Process Voice Bigger Zama operations use “acid baths” where highly volatile and even deadly chemicals like cyanide are added to the mix to separate the gold from the ore. In the final stage, gold concentrate will be brought to smelting houses like these where the resulting nugget can sell at upwards of R1000 per gram at Zama prices. Upsound Masa This is a precious natural resource area - but look at the state it’s in. Upsound destroy camp Voice Security do what they can to disrupt the operation – unable to catch them, they try to discourage them from coming back. Upsound destroy camp and fire Voice As this illegal camp goes up in flames, 60 kms away, close to Mpumalanga’s capital, another is flourishing. Upsound Mongezi Mlambo The kinds of guns that these guys carry, it’s the kinds of guns that you’ll see on Rambo. Or on big action movies. Voice In Mashabotho - just outside Mbombela - a rural community is living in fear. Upsound Mongezi Mlambo Sometimes you have to pass through the bushes, because you can’t use an open road. Because they will see you from far, and attack you. Voice People here make a humble living from working a farm government handed back to them after a successful land claim. Upsound Mongezi It was just the communities and the beneficiaries living here. It was peaceful. Voice Mashabotho local, Mongezi Mlambo, says a nearby hillside, part of their land, has been invaded by zamas, interrupting their plans to get the farm up and running. Upsound Mongezi goes up? Masa: The crime aspect, would you say that as the zamas increase in the area the crime also Mongezi: It’s the reason why there’s crime. Voice It’s a view we’ve encountered all over the Lowveld: where Zama Zamas gather, crime inevitably increases. Upsound Mongezi Mongezi: We had local spazas here that were operating, all these things closed because of these guys. So these guys will come and own that place. Sort of like remove you from that place and say ok, from today, you’re no longer occupying here. If we find you tomorrow we’re gonna abuse you up until you on your own say I no longer want to continue. Masa: Tell us how that has impacted this community? Mongezi: It has destroyed a lot of lives. Day and night, they are not safe. Voice Eager to get a glimpse of the operation that’s brought business here to a halt, we attempt to negotiate our way up the hillside. Link Masa Up on this mountain there are literally hundreds of zamas operating - we also wanted to hear their side of the story - but the syndicate leaders didn’t give us permission. Instead, they sent two men down here to meet with us. Voice One of them, whose name is Surprise, agrees to talk to us. He’s left behind a corporate life for the better paying Zama life. Upsound “Surprise” Masa: Did you study? Surprise: Yes, I did study. Masa: What did you study? Surprise: Oﬃce administration. Masa: Oﬃce administration. And you work underground? Surprise: I am happy because I’ve got like certain targets that I have to reach, but I’m going to do it temporarily, it’s not going to be forever you see. Voice He tells us there’s more gold available here than in Gauteng. Upsound Surpise Masa: How much money do you make out of this on average? Surprise: Last week we were working, and then we are going to be coming out this Saturday - so it’s going to be two weeks full that we’re working, so maybe plus minus R20 000 for me. And we’re a syndicate you see. Upsound Mongezi There are big guys that are benefitting from this, and that is why whenever you report such cases, they always go unsolved. Voice Mongezi believes powerful people are shielding the Zamas from justice. Surprise might make 20 thousand, but the syndicate bosses make far more. Upsound Mongezi Because of the involvement of very influential people from within the country. Which is the sad story. Upsound Surpise Masa: Everywhere where there’s communities living where the zamas are as well, they’re living in fear. They’re saying as zamas you’re disturbing them. You’re actually harassing them. What do you say to that? Surprise: On the bad side of it is like we are working with illegal people, we’ve got like ammunition, and obviously when we’re digging, obviously even us, we have to explode… so obviously it disturbs the people that are not used to such type of a vibe of maybe explosions, guns triggering every now and then. Masa: And the zama’s here, you don’t think they harass the community members here? Surpise: No, they don’t harass the community members here. ACT 3 Voice This area is the country’s second biggest producer of citrus fruits and the “acid baths” used by the zamas are threatening water sources vital to the sector’s survival. And, as we discover first hand in Barberton, a little over 40 kms away, famed World Heritage Sites aren’t being spared either. Upsound Masa How much further? Voice history. Famous for its gold mines and as the home of Jock of the Bushveld, Baberton has a rich cultural Upsound Masa One thing about the zama world, there’s a lot of walking, you need to be fit. Voice We’re trekking up a mountain just outside the town, following a pair of illegal miners who’ve agreed to show us their operations. Upsound Masa Masa: Welcome to zama zama land. Zama: Don’t run away, we spoke to security when we arrived. Link Masa It’s not that easy entering the world of the zama zamas. There’s a lot of layers to get through to get the permission to be in this space. Right now, there are zamas on the mountain as we’re waiting to get our final permission. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A fact finding mission to Pilgrim's Rest to investigate zama zama activity leads to an alarming expose' - has the Lowveld been hijacked by illegal miners?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We spent a day in the sleepy tourist town of Pilgrim's rest, where our producer went undercover as a tourist taking in the sights. We'd heard reports of zama activity in the area, and that the situation had become dangerous for tourists. Although Pilgrim's is by no means overrun by zama zamas, they can be found in the town, processing gold bearing material at the river just 500 meters away from the main tourist attractions. But our producer dug a little a deeper, and has uncovered that the illegal mining problem in the Lowveld is possibly even bigger than what residents in places like Guateng's West and East Rand are dealing with. With the surge in zama activity, major tourist hotspots in the Lowveld are on the brink of disaster - as the illegal mining in the area has caused a sharp increase in violent crimes, and just as concerning, a major ecological threat to our natural heritage in the area. Illegal miners are constructing so called "Cyanide Baths" next to important waterways such as the Sabie and Crocodile river, using deadly poisons such as cyanide in the process of processing the gold ore.
metadata.Summary: We have access to never before seen areas where large scale zama zama activities are taking place in the Lowveld. We have been given a lot of exclusive footage of zama operations as well. We have access to sources working on intelligence gathering on zama operations - who can open this hidden world. We will show the scale of the problems in areas such as Nelspruit, Sabie, Pilgrim's Rest, Waterval Onder and Barberton. In e each town we have insiders who can give us exclusive access into the hidden world of the zamas.
